name: Federal Way
headline: Federal Way: a plateau city between Puget Sound and the Green River Valley, now on the Link 1 Line.
lede: Federal Way sits in the southwest corner of King County, about 25 miles south of downtown Seattle and eight miles north of downtown Tacoma. This guide covers getting around, parks and the shoreline, schools, everyday errands, housing and zoning, and what’s nearby, with a source for every fact.

notes: Population and area differ by source. The Census Bureau counts 101,030 people in 2020 and 22.30 square miles of land; the City’s profile page says 101,300 people and about 21.5 square miles. This guide uses the Census figures.

The City’s park figures differ between its own pages: the City Profile lists 31 developed and 19 open space parks covering about 1,141 acres, while the About page says 33 developed parks in a 1,094-acre system. The guide uses the City Profile numbers.

Sound Transit’s opening release gives about 46 minutes from Federal Way Downtown to Seattle; Wikipedia gives about 56 minutes to Westlake. The guide uses Sound Transit’s 16 minutes to the airport and leaves the Seattle time general.
Wikipedia’s Federal Way article says Federal Way High School opened in 1930; the Federal Way Public Schools article says 1938. Neither date is used.

Wild Waves was announced to close permanently on November 1, 2026. The sources checked state the planned date; no source was found confirming the closing day itself or a new use for the land, which the property owner called preliminary.

Census housing, rent and commute figures are 2020–2024 American Community Survey estimates as shown on QuickFacts when checked. The PAEC’s City page is older and still describes the building as under construction; its August 2017 opening comes from Wikipedia.
Left out because no fetched source stated them clearly: a full list of cities bordering Federal Way, electric and gas utility providers, and Lakehaven’s exact service boundary.

chapters.title: Getting around and commutes
chapters.intro: I-5 and Pacific Highway South run the length of Federal Way, and Link light rail now reaches downtown. Census figures put the mean travel time to work for Federal Way residents at 32.1 minutes (2020–2024).
items: The 7.8-mile Federal Way Link Extension opened December 6, 2025, with new stations at Kent Des Moines, Star Lake and Federal Way Downtown. Trains run every 8 minutes at peak, about 16 minutes to Sea-Tac Airport.
At 31621 23rd Avenue South, with 13 bus bays and a five-story garage of 1,500 stalls. King County Metro, Pierce Transit and Sound Transit Express buses serve it.
In southwestern Kent near I-5 and South 272nd Street, with a 1,100-space garage, King County Metro and Sound Transit Express buses. It opened with the extension on December 6, 2025.
Runs about 11 miles on Pacific Highway South (SR 99) between Tukwila International Boulevard station and Federal Way Downtown station, every 10 minutes at peak and every 15 minutes off-peak.
I-5 enters Federal Way after climbing out of the Puyallup River valley, running parallel to SR 99. The HOV lanes have a direct off-ramp to the transit center and The Commons at Federal Way.
Starts as South 348th Street at SR 99 and runs northeast, mostly as a freeway, through Auburn, Kent, Covington and Maple Valley to I-90 west of North Bend. It is 28.41 miles long.
SR 509 travels east as Dash Point Road through Federal Way, passing Decatur and Federal Way high schools before meeting SR 99. To the west it runs through Dash Point toward Tacoma.

chapters.title: Parks and outdoors
chapters.intro: Federal Way’s parks run from a Puget Sound state park and a wetland preserve to lakes, ballfields and the BPA Trail. The City lists about 1,141 acres of parks and open space.
items: At 5700 SW Dash Point Road, with 461 acres, 3,301 feet of saltwater shoreline, forested hiking and biking trails, camping and cabins. Wikipedia calls it the only developed waterfront park within city limits.
A 52-acre park at 2410 South 312th Street with a swimming beach, skate park, playground, sand volleyball, seasonal fishing and a boat launch.
83.5 acres at 1095 South 324th Street, with four lighted baseball fields, four lighted soccer fields, a playground and about 1.88 miles of trails connecting to the BPA Trail.
A 120-acre park at 411 South 348th Street with interpretive nature trails, observation platforms and about 1.01 miles of trail.
A walking and biking path of about 3.64 miles that connects parks and neighborhoods across the city.
A 3.91-acre downtown park at 31600 Pete von Reichbauer Way South, with a splash pad, playground and open lawn.
10 acres at 31531 1st Avenue South. The City says it is the only City park where off-leash use is approved.
Moved to Federal Way in 1974 on land provided by Weyerhaeuser’s headquarters. It covers 22 to 24 acres, sits next to the Pacific Bonsai Museum, and held 850 rhododendron species by 2019.

chapters.title: Schools
chapters.intro: Federal Way Public Schools covers all of Federal Way, plus parts of Kent, Des Moines and Auburn. Boundaries change; confirm school assignment with the district for any specific address.
items: Covers 35 square miles in King County, with 21 elementary, 3 K–8, 6 middle and 4 high schools listed. The district was formed on May 22, 1929, when five small districts consolidated.
Federal Way takes its name from the school district, which adopted the name of U.S. Route 99, the federal highway, when it consolidated in 1929.
The district’s planning nights list Todd Beamer, Federal Way, Decatur and Thomas Jefferson (in Auburn) high schools, plus Career Academy at Truman, TAF@Saghalie, Internet Academy and Open Doors.
Federal Way Public Academy serves grades 6–10 and TAF@Saghalie grades 6–12. The district also requires 24 hours of community service to graduate, adopted in 2021.
The district’s School Lookup Tool finds the neighborhood school for a home address, and its Enrollment Support Team can help.
Families can apply for a school outside their assigned attendance area if space allows. Approval is not guaranteed, and families provide transportation to a Choice school.

chapters.title: Everyday errands
chapters.intro: Downtown Federal Way, around South 320th Street and Pacific Highway South, holds the mall, a library, the transit hub and the performing arts center.
items: The city’s only indoor shopping center, at 1928 South Commons. It opened August 14, 1975, as SeaTac Mall and was renamed in 2003; Target and Kohl’s are among its anchors.
The King County Library System’s Federal Way 320th branch is at 848 South 320th Street; its current building opened in September 2013.
A second King County Library System branch opened in 1991 and was expanded to 34,500 square feet in 2010.
St. Francis Hospital at 34515 9th Avenue South offers emergency services 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and a family birth center.
South King Fire provides fire, emergency medical and rescue service to Federal Way and Des Moines, with headquarters at 31617 1st Avenue South.
Waste Management handles residential curbside service: garbage weekly, recycling every other week, and optional weekly yard and food waste.
Lakehaven Water and Sewer District has served the Federal Way area for more than 50 years, with about 400 miles of mainline and 22 wells.
Saturdays, May through September, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m., on the Civic Plaza Lawn next to the Performing Arts and Event Center.

chapters.title: Housing and neighborhoods
chapters.intro: Federal Way began as a logging settlement and grew along Highway 99, then I-5. Today its code allows several homes per single-family lot, and new housing is planned beside the light rail station.
items: Owner-occupied housing rate 55.3%, median owner-occupied home value $552,800 and median gross rent $1,797 (Census, 2020–2024).
The first homestead was established in 1871 near today’s Redondo. I-5 opened through the area in October 1962, and the city annexed the Northlake, East Redondo and Parkway neighborhoods in 2004.
The RS zones run from RS 35.0 (35,000-square-foot minimum lots) through RS 15.0, RS 9.6 and RS 7.2 down to RS 5.0 (5,000 square feet).
A single-family lot may hold up to six homes, as middle housing or a mix with a house and ADUs, limited by water and sewer. Up to two ADUs per lot are allowed, each up to 1,000 square feet.
Where only on-site septic serves an area, the code caps development at two units per lot until sewer is available. Ask about sewer or septic for any specific property.

Sound Transit plans about 230 homes in two buildings on vacant land next to Federal Way Downtown station, for households earning 30% to 60% of area median income. Developers aim to break ground in 2028.
The Performing Arts and Event Center, a 44,000-square-foot building with a two-tiered, 716-seat theatre, sits at South 316th Street and Pete von Reichbauer Way South.

chapters.title: What’s nearby
chapters.intro: Federal Way borders Des Moines to the north and Auburn’s West Hill to the east, with the Pierce County line to the south and Puget Sound to the west.
items: Borders Federal Way to the north, with 32,888 people in 2020. It has a city marina with 838 berths, Highline College and the Kent Des Moines light rail station.

Auburn’s West Hill borders Federal Way. The city counted 87,256 people in 2020 and has a Sounder station with trains to downtown Seattle in about 30 minutes, plus Emerald Downs and The Outlet Collection.
Lies in northern Pierce County and southern King County, with 8,697 people in 2020. Federal Way Public Schools serves parts of its King County portion.
An unincorporated Pierce County community of 963 people (2020), north of Tacoma across Commencement Bay. Dash Point State Park borders it on the King County side.
Opened April 18, 1990, with an Olympic-size competition pool and a 17-foot diving well. It has hosted U.S. Olympic Diving Team Trials and NCAA championships.
The theme and water park at 36201 Enchanted Parkway South opened in 1977 as The Enchanted Village. Its owner announced it would close permanently on November 1, 2026, after the 2026 season.
